faqs.heading: Frequently Asked Questions
faqs.q1: How quickly can I renew my passport?
faqs.a1: Processing times and any expedited options depend on the issuing authority and can change. Check its current instructions before applying.
faqs.q2: What documents do I need to renew my passport?
faqs.a2: You will generally need your most recent passport book, a compliant passport photo, the appropriate government application form, and required government fees.
faqs.q3: Can I travel while my passport is being renewed?
faqs.a3: No. When you submit your current passport for renewal, it is surrendered until the new passport is issued and returned to you.
faqs.q4: Are government fees included in service pricing?
faqs.a4: Government fees are statutory payments mandated by issuing authorities and are listed separately from document preparation and concierge fees.
faqs.q5: What happens if my application has an error?
faqs.a5: Our team reviews your forms and documentation before submission to catch common mistakes, omissions, and photo non-compliance.

cta.title: Ready to get your passport sorted?
cta.body: Start your intake in minutes. We will verify your documentation and guide every step.

meta.title: New Passport Assistance — Visa Expeditor
meta.description: First-time passport application help: identity documents, forms, photos and submission steps.

hero.heading: New Passport Assistance
hero.subhead: Prepare a first-time passport application with the right identity documents and a reviewed form.

overview.heading: What this service covers
overview.p1: A first passport proves your identity and citizenship, usually for an adult or a child applying for the first time. The exact documents depend on your country and your circumstances.
overview.p2: We help you confirm what to provide, prepare the supporting evidence and review the form before submission.

whoFor.heading: Who this is for
whoFor.i1: Adults applying for their first passport.
whoFor.i2: Parents or guardians applying for a child.
whoFor.i3: Applicants unsure which identity documents are accepted.

s1.title: Confirm the requirements
s1.description: We check what your country asks of first-time applicants, including for minors.

s2.title: Gather identity documents
s2.description: We help you collect proof of identity, citizenship and any parental consent.

s3.title: Complete the application
s3.description: We review the form and photo against the official requirements.

s4.title: Submit and wait
s4.description: You submit through the official channel and we explain the expected stages.

r1.label: Photos
r1.value: Compliant passport photographs for each applicant.

r3.label: Proof of citizenship
r3.value: A birth certificate or equivalent, as your country requires.

r4.label: Application form
r4.value: The completed official form, signed as required.

faqs.heading: Frequently Asked Questions
faqs.a1: Usually a birth certificate or an equivalent record. The accepted evidence depends on your country and situation.
faqs.q2: Can I apply for my child?
faqs.a2: Yes. Minors generally need additional consent and evidence of the parent or guardian's identity.
faqs.q3: How long is a first passport valid?
faqs.a3: Validity periods vary by country and by the applicant's age. Check the rule that applies to you.
faqs.q4: What if I have no birth certificate?
faqs.a4: Alternative evidence may be accepted. Tell us your situation and we will help you identify what to provide.
faqs.q5: Do I need to apply in person?
faqs.a5: Some countries require an in-person appointment for first passports. We explain what your destination requires.

cta.title: Applying for the first time?
cta.body: Tell us about your case and we will prepare the documents involved.

meta.title: Passport Renewal Assistance — Visa Expeditor
meta.description: Renew an expiring or recently expired passport with a checked application and organized supporting documents.

hero.heading: Passport Renewal Assistance
hero.subhead: Renew an expiring or recently expired passport with a reviewed application.

overview.heading: What this service covers
overview.p1: Renewing keeps your passport current and avoids last-minute problems at the airport. Most countries allow renewal before expiry, and some allow a short grace period after.
overview.p2: We help you confirm you qualify for renewal, prepare the required items and review the form before you submit.

whoFor.heading: Who this is for
whoFor.i1: Holders of a passport nearing expiry.
whoFor.i2: Travelers with a recently expired passport.
whoFor.i3: Anyone whose destination requires more validity than their passport has.

s1.title: Check eligibility
s1.description: We confirm whether your passport qualifies for renewal or needs a different process.

s2.title: Prepare documents and photo
s2.description: We help you gather the current passport, photo and any supporting evidence.

s3.title: Complete the renewal form
s3.description: We review the form for accuracy and consistency with your details.

s4.title: Submit and get status updates by email
s4.description: You submit through the official channel and we explain what happens next.

r1.label: Current passport
r1.value: Your existing passport, which is usually surrendered during renewal.

r2.label: Photo
r2.value: A recent photograph meeting the current specifications.

r3.label: Application form
r3.value: The completed renewal form for your country.

r4.label: Name-change evidence
r4.value: Supporting documents if your name or details have changed.

faqs.heading: Frequently Asked Questions
faqs.a1: Renew before your passport fails a destination's validity rule. Many travelers renew within a year of expiry.
faqs.q2: Can I renew a recently expired passport?
faqs.a2: Many countries allow renewal after expiry within a limited period. Check the rule that applies to your passport.
faqs.q3: Can I travel while it is being renewed?
faqs.a3: Usually not, because your current passport is surrendered or invalidated during the process.
faqs.q4: Do I need a new photo?
faqs.a4: Yes, in most cases. Photos must meet the current requirements and cannot be reused from an old passport.
faqs.q5: What if my details have changed?
faqs.a5: A name or detail change may need supporting evidence or a different application. Tell us and we will advise.

cta.title: Passport up for renewal?
cta.body: Talk to us and we will prepare a clean renewal application.

meta.title: Passport Name Change Assistance — Visa Expeditor
meta.description: Update your passport after marriage, divorce or a legal name change with the right supporting evidence.

hero.heading: Passport Name Change Assistance
hero.subhead: Update your passport after marriage, divorce or a legal name change with verified evidence.

overview.heading: What this service covers
overview.p1: A name change updates your passport to match a legal name change, such as marriage, divorce or a court order. The accepted evidence depends on your country.
overview.p2: We help you identify the documents that support the change and prepare a consistent application.

whoFor.heading: Who this is for
whoFor.i1: People who changed their name through marriage or divorce.
whoFor.i2: Applicants with a court-ordered name change.
whoFor.i3: Travelers whose passport details no longer match other documents.

s1.title: Confirm the evidence
s1.description: We identify which document supports your change of name.

s2.title: Prepare the documents
s2.description: We help you gather the certificate, order or record required.

s3.title: Complete the application
s3.description: We review the form so the new name matches your evidence exactly.

s4.title: Submit and get status updates by email
s4.description: You submit through the official channel and we explain the next steps.

r1.label: Current passport
r1.value: Your existing passport, where the change is an amendment or renewal.

r2.label: Marriage or divorce record
r2.value: The certificate that shows the change, where relevant.

r3.label: Court order
r3.value: A legal name-change order, where applicable.

r4.label: Photo
r4.value: A recent photograph meeting the current specifications.

faqs.heading: Frequently Asked Questions
faqs.q1: Which document proves a name change?
faqs.a1: A marriage certificate, divorce decree or court order, depending on the change. The accepted document varies by country.
faqs.q2: Do I need a new passport or an amendment?
faqs.a2: It depends on your country and how much time remains on your passport. We can help you work out which applies.
faqs.q3: Can I keep my old passport?
faqs.a3: Often the old passport is cancelled or returned with a hole punch. The rule depends on your country.
faqs.a4: Processing times vary by country and season and change over time, so apply as early as you can.
faqs.q5: What if my tickets are in the old name?
faqs.a5: Travel documents should match your passport name. Contact your airline about updating the booking before you travel.

cta.title: Changed your name?
cta.body: Send us the details and we will prepare the evidence and forms.

meta.title: Lost or Stolen Passport Assistance — Visa Expeditor
meta.description: Report and replace a lost, stolen or damaged passport with clear steps and organized documents.

hero.heading: Lost, Stolen or Damaged Passport
hero.subhead: Report and replace a lost, stolen or damaged passport with clear, organized steps.

overview.heading: What this service covers
overview.p1: If your passport is lost, stolen or damaged, report it as soon as you can so it cannot be misused, then apply for a replacement. The steps differ depending on whether you are at home or abroad.
overview.p2: We help you understand the reporting and replacement process and prepare the supporting documents it requires.

whoFor.heading: Who this is for
whoFor.i1: Travelers who have lost or had a passport stolen.
whoFor.i2: Holders of a damaged passport that is no longer valid.
whoFor.i3: People planning a replacement before upcoming travel.

s1.title: Report the loss
s1.description: We explain how to report the passport so it cannot be used by anyone else.

s2.title: Gather supporting documents
s2.description: We help you collect identity, citizenship and, if relevant, police documents.

s3.title: Complete the replacement application
s3.description: We review the form and evidence before you submit.

s4.title: Submit and get status updates by email
s4.description: You submit through the official channel and we explain the timeline and options.

r1.label: Police report
r1.value: A report, where the passport was stolen or the country requires one.

r2.label: Proof of identity
r2.value: A recognized identity document or a copy of the lost passport.

r3.label: Proof of citizenship
r3.value: A birth certificate or equivalent, as required.

r4.label: Photo
r4.value: A recent photograph meeting the current specifications.

faqs.heading: Frequently Asked Questions
faqs.a1: Report the passport as lost or stolen to the relevant authority as soon as possible, then begin the replacement process.
faqs.q2: Do I need a police report?
faqs.a2: For a stolen passport, usually yes. For a lost passport, requirements vary by country.
faqs.q3: Can I travel with a damaged passport?
faqs.a3: A damaged passport may be refused at the border. If it is damaged, treat it as invalid and apply for a replacement.
faqs.q4: How long does a replacement take?
faqs.a4: Timelines vary by country and urgency and change over time. Tell us your travel date and we will help you plan.
faqs.q5: Can I get an emergency passport?
faqs.a5: Some countries issue emergency travel documents for urgent cases. Availability and eligibility depend on your country.

cta.title: Lost or damaged your passport?
cta.body: Contact us and we will help you plan the replacement.
